A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same FLEX-Judge study with complete main text and Appendices A–E. Extracted text, tables and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original multimodal judge evaluations, molecular best-of-N and DPO experiments, and ablation and supplementary results in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results, including multimodal benchmarking, molecular applications and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 retains the same 1K textual-reasoning dataset curation, fine-tuning and zero-shot judging procedure. The molecular adaptation and best-of-N/DPO procedures also remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The image, video, audio, molecular and text task coverage is unchanged. Appendix C retains the same additional benchmarks and TextVQA/OK-VQA evaluations; no dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain identical baseline sets, including GPT-4o, Gemini variants, LLaVA-Critic-7B, Prometheus-Vision-13B and Qwen backbones. Comparator membership also matches throughout the appendix tables.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix B retain identical training settings, sample sizes, evaluation prompts, scoring and ranking metrics, and bias-handling procedures. No evaluation protocol is introduced or revised.

E4.justification: The seed-curation analyses, reasoning ablation, inference-time scaling and data-quality comparison are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same model-size, bias and forgetting analyses, and Appendix D retains the same qualitative cases.

E5.justification: Repeated-sampling information remains identical: three samples for MLLM-as-a-Judge and five for VL-RewardBench in Table 6, and ten random molecular best-of-N trials in Appendix B.4.1. Uncertainty displays are also unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout both PDFs. For example, FLEX-VL-7B retains 48.60 overall accuracy on VL-RewardBench in Table 2, and molecular DPO retains 80.10% accuracy in Figure 4.

T1.justification: The existing mathematical content, including the DPO preference-triplet notation, is unchanged. Neither version presents formal theorems or proofs, and no new mathematical reasoning is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about minimal text-only supervision enabling multimodal judging, competitive evaluation performance, and molecular best-of-N selection and preference optimization.

C2.justification: Interpretations of reasoning transfer, data quality and model scale remain unchanged. Appendix E retains the reasoning-capable-backbone requirement and failed 3D-LLM adaptation attributed to limited context and weak reasoning pretraining.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the first-page direct code-repository link with the project website already cited in the appendices. This revises the access pointer; implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters and resource-release statements remain unchanged. Actual resource availability changes are not established.

R1.justification: All 91 references and the research positioning in Section 6 and Appendix A are unchanged. Bibliography entries move across pages without adding or removing cited works.

P1.justification: v4 updates Jongwoo Ko’s affiliation and contact information, adds conference identification, and inserts funding and contributor acknowledgements. Scientific prose and the main-text and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–17 and Tables 1–11 retain their content, structure and captions. The revised author block, conference footer and added acknowledgements cause limited layout changes and bibliography reflow.

improvement.justification: The scientific argument, empirical evidence, experimental reproducibility details and limitations remain unchanged. Added acknowledgements and updated affiliation, contact and project-link information improve administrative completeness, but do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
